title: Service as worship
hook: God says, I was sick and you did not visit Me: how could God be sick?
tomorrow: do you have to be an expert before you share?

segments.voice: Yesterday: they are communities too, every creature a people. Today's puzzle sounds almost impossible, and it closes this stretch on service.
screen: `THEY ARE COMMUNITIES TOO.` → `A PUZZLE TO CLOSE THE STRETCH.`

segments.voice: Service hours. A form, a supervisor's signature, a number for an application. Some service gets logged. Some never does. In a hadith in Sahih Muslim, God speaks, and keeps the log in the oddest way. On the Day of Judgment, God says: O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me. The man is baffled. How could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds? Fair question. How could God be sick?
screen: `SOME SERVICE GETS LOGGED.` → `I WAS SICK, AND YOU DID NOT VISIT ME.` → `HOW COULD GOD BE SICK?`

segments.voice: God's answer solves it. My servant so-and-so was sick, and you did not visit him. Didn't you know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him? Then twice more. I asked you for food and you didn't feed Me. I asked you for water and you gave Me none. Each time the same answer: had you fed him, had you given him drink, you would have found that with Me. So God isn't sick. God is with the sick. The visit you skipped was a visit you could have made to Him. That's inside today's line: service with the right intention is prayer in action. The hadith that opens Sahih al-Bukhari says it plainly: actions are only by intentions, and each person gets what they intended. Two people carry the same box of groceries to a neighbor. For one, it's hours for a form. For the other, it's also a visit to someone God is with. The box weighs the same. What it is depends on why. This isn't a rule against logging hours. Some Muslims say a quiet bismillah, in the name of God, before a task, which turns an errand toward worship without changing the errand at all.
screen: `MY SERVANT WAS SICK.` · `YOU'D HAVE FOUND ME WITH HIM.` · `ACTIONS ARE BY INTENTIONS.` · `SAME BOX, DIFFERENT WHY.` · then, large: `SERVICE IS PRAYER.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one ordinary task waiting for you today: dishes, an email, a shift. Hold it there without changing it, and ask quietly what it would become if you did it for God's sake, or for the person it helps. Stay with that answer until the time is up.
screen: `ONE ORDINARY TASK.` · `THE SAME TASK, A NEW WHY.`

segments.voice: Service as worship: helping people with the right intention, so the help itself becomes prayer. In the hadith, God is with the sick.
Your line: service is prayer. Same box of groceries, carried with a different why. Peace for now.

screen: `DAY 1745 COUNTS.` → `SERVICE AND JUSTICE · 10 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: DO YOU HAVE TO BE AN EXPERT TO SHARE?`

howItsDone: Muslims speak of setting the intention (niyyah) before good work, and some say bismillah before a task; visiting the sick, feeding people and giving water are counted as worship when done for God's sake.

fork.setup: you're taking soup to a sick roommate and you're annoyed about it the whole way there. is it still worth bringing?
options: bring it, and turn the why on the way: God is with the sick, the hadith says.
skip it; if your heart isn't in it, the act counts for nothing at all.
bring it, but it's only a favor; worship is what happens on a prayer mat.
fork.reveal: God says: had you visited him, you would have found Me with him. the act is right, and the intention can be turned on the way.

original.note: Arabic: intention, what you mean by an act. actions are only by intentions.

trapdoor: what you thought: worship happens on a prayer mat; service is something else.
what it means: in the hadith, God is with the sick, the hungry and the thirsty; serving them for His sake is worship.
what a scholar hears: Muslim 2569 is a hadith qudsi, God speaking in the first person; scholars read it with Bukhari 1, innama al-a'malu bin-niyyat, actions are only by intentions.
guess: helping people for God's sake, as worship
working full time for a mosque or charity
praying for people instead of helping them

chat.says: the pantry shifts count for my scholarship hours. does that ruin it? like is it fake service now?
options: Not fake. Actions go by intentions; keep God's sake at the center and log the hours.
Yes. Once it counts for anything else, the reward is gone, so stop logging it.
Doesn't matter. Service is service; why you do it never changes what it is.
chat.meaning: Actions are by intentions. Service done for God's sake is worship; in the hadith, God is with the one you serve.

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major collection of the Prophet's sayings and deeds

Sahih al-Bukhari.meaning: a major collection of reports of the Prophet's words and deeds
